source_evidence: Many ETFs invest in a range of companies and industries rather than investing in one specific stock or bond. This helps to lower your risk if one company fails. However, some ETFs are less diverse than others.
answer: Diversification means an ETF holds investments across multiple companies or industries instead of relying on a single investment. This can lower the impact of one company failing. But ETFs vary: some hold fewer investments, and some may even track a single stock, so they can be concentrated rather than broadly diversified. Diversification does not remove all risk; the value of a fund’s holdings can still fall.
